s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with increasing severity and evidence of intra-abdominal hemorrhage
salient_findings: Paroxysmal abdominal pain increasing in severity
Tenderness in the left lower quadrant of the abdomen
Intra-abdominal hemorrhage and pseudoaneurysm formation on imaging
key_facts: 50-year-old male patient
Presented with paroxysmal abdominal pain for 4 days
Pain intensity increased in the left lower abdomen 7 hours after admission
No history of fever, weight loss, pancreatitis, surgery, hematochezia, vascular diseases, or previous angiography
Blood pressure: 145/91 mmHg
Heart rate: 93 beats/min
Respiratory rate: 20 breaths/min
Hemoglobin level: 8.2 g/dl
Serum amylase level: normal
Abdominal ultrasonography revealed massive fluid collection in the abdomen
Abdominal CT showed nodular contrast medium staining and extravasation, intra-abdominal hemorrhage, pseudoaneurysm formation, and multiple hematoceles
Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA) confirmed pseudoaneurysm formation, 4 mm in diameter, arising from the left branch of the inferior mesenteric artery

s4.champion: Pseudoaneurysm of the inferior mesenteric artery

raw.champion: Pseudoaneurysm of the inferior mesenteric artery
raw.rationale: The patient's abdominal CT and DSA results confirm pseudoaneurysm formation, 4 mm in diameter, arising from the left branch of the inferior mesenteric artery, which explains the intra-abdominal hemorrhage and hematoceles.

rejected.label: Inferior mesenteric artery aneurysm
rejected.why: While related, the specific diagnosis of pseudoaneurysm is more accurate based on the imaging findings.

rejected.label: Intra-abdominal hemorrhage
rejected.why: This is a symptom rather than a primary diagnosis, as it is caused by the pseudoaneurysm.

rejected.label: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm
rejected.why: The location and source of the bleeding are specified as the left branch of the inferior mesenteric artery, not the abdominal aorta.

rejected.label: Intestinal angiodysplasia
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence provided in the case facts to support this diagnosis, which typically presents with recurrent bleeding and is often associated with aortic stenosis or other conditions not mentioned here.
